requirements.title: Add project-map freshness and changelog-drift checks to omni doctor
requirements.description: Two generic omni doctor checks, developed while auditing an adopter project (STEP) for OmniEngineering alignment and ported back here so every adopter benefits: validate_project_map_freshness warns when a top-level directory that exists on disk is missing from .ai/project-map.md's tree (catches a map that was never regenerated after a structural change); validate_recent_commits_tracked warns when commits postdate -- by commit timestamp, not git log X..HEAD DAG reachability, which squash-merge PR histories make misleading -- the last commit that touched CHANGELOG.md, naming each one so untracked work is caught automatically instead of by manual audit.
acceptance_criteria: omni doctor warns when an ALLOWED_ROOT_DIRS directory present on disk is absent from the generated project map's directory tree.
omni doctor warns, listing each commit, when commits postdate (by commit date) the last commit that touched CHANGELOG.md.
Both checks are no-ops (skip silently) when git or the relevant files are unavailable, so they never turn into false errors on a non-git or freshly-adopted workspace.
risk_notes: The commit-date comparison intentionally avoids `git log <hash>..HEAD` because squash-merge PR workflows make already-integrated side-branch commits appear "after" the changelog commit in DAG-reachability terms even though they landed chronologically earlier; using commit timestamps instead avoids that false positive.

requirements.title: Wire omni doctor into CI and stop future line-ending drift
requirements.description: Two efficiency/maintainability fixes identified while discussing how to make OmniEngineering easier to integrate and keep aligned over time: (1) added .github/workflows/ci.yml running `python3 omni doctor` (full-history checkout) on every push/PR to main, so workspace-health drift is caught automatically instead of relying on someone manually running the command or an LLM session auditing on request; (2) added .gitattributes (`* text=auto eol=lf`) so a Windows/WSL checkout stops silently diverging from committed line endings -- this repo's entire working tree had drifted to CRLF against an LF-committed history, which was masking real diffs behind whole-file noise.
acceptance_criteria: omni doctor runs automatically on every push and pull request to main and fails the build only on real errors, not warnings.
.gitattributes normalizes text files to LF so future checkouts don't silently drift from committed line endings.
Existing committed content is left untouched -- .gitattributes affects future checkouts/commits, not a retroactive rewrite.
risk_notes: This repo's existing tracked files are still CRLF in the working tree as of this change; .gitattributes stops new drift but does not retroactively renormalize what's already committed. A follow-up `git add --renormalize .` commit would fix that but was intentionally left out of scope here since it would touch every file in the repo.

requirements.title: Add omni update: 3-way-merge template improvements into adopted workspaces
requirements.description: The single biggest 'clunky' gap raised this session: once a project adopts OmniEngineering and customizes its rules/playbooks/checklists, there was no way to pull later template improvements in except a manual hand-diff-and-port (done twice by hand earlier this session). Adds .ai/omni-version.json (written by omni adopt, recording the source path and git ref at last sync) and a new 'omni update --source <checkout>' command that 3-way-merges every template-managed file via git merge-file: files the adopter never touched are fast-path overwritten, files only the template changed are left alone, files both sides changed are merged (or left with conflict markers on a genuine collision), and .ai/project-configuration.md, .ai/project-map.md, .ai/requirements/requirements.json, and CHANGELOG.md are never touched since those are adopter-owned. If make_ai.py itself changes, update automatically re-runs sync in a fresh process so entrypoint/pointer/ignore files regenerate from the new templates. omni doctor gained a matching check warning when .ai/omni-version.json is missing. Also adds `--bootstrap` to `omni update` (records --source's current ref as the starting point without merging anything, for a workspace adopted before update-tracking existed) and a README Quick Start section covering the adopt/doctor/update loop end to end, including the bootstrap path, since a working feature nobody can find or follow doesn't solve the 'clunky to integrate' complaint either.
acceptance_criteria: omni adopt writes .ai/omni-version.json on success.

omni update fast-path-overwrites adopter-untouched files, no-ops on adopter-only changes, cleanly merges non-overlapping changes on both sides, and leaves conflict markers on overlapping changes -- verified end to end in a scratch adopter workspace covering all four cases plus confirming requirements.json/project-map.md/project-configuration.md/CHANGELOG.md are never touched.
omni update --bootstrap writes .ai/omni-version.json against --source's current ref and merges nothing, verified end to end.
omni doctor warns when .ai/omni-version.json is missing.
README Quick Start section documents adopt, doctor, update, and the bootstrap path for pre-existing adopters.
risk_notes: Requires --source to be a real git checkout (needed to reconstruct the 3-way-merge base via git show); a plain folder copy as source is explicitly rejected with a clear message rather than guessing.
Fetching a template source directly from a remote git URL is an intentional follow-up, not included here -- v1 matches omni adopt's existing local-checkout-path convention.

requirements.title: Fix: omni update must not re-run sync when make_ai.py itself has an unresolved conflict
requirements.description: Found live while dogfooding REQ-013 against STEP_App's genuinely diverged make_ai.py: when make_ai.py's own merge produced a conflict, the file was written with unresolved <<<<<<< markers (correct), but run_update still treated that as make_ai.py having 'changed' and re-ran sync in a fresh subprocess against the now-syntactically-invalid file, producing a raw Python SyntaxError traceback instead of a clean message. Excluded the conflict outcome from the make_ai_changed re-sync trigger, and added an explicit message telling the user sync was skipped and why, and to run it themselves once the conflict is resolved.
acceptance_criteria: omni update no longer attempts to re-run sync when make_ai.py itself has an unresolved conflict; prints a clear explanatory message instead of a raw traceback. Verified by reproducing the original crash against STEP_App before the fix and confirming a clean message after.

requirements.title: Add omni graph: a deterministic tree-sitter AST code graph, not a vector index
requirements.description: Adds `omni graph build/trace/show`, a new omni_graph.py module holding a local, deterministic code graph parsed from source with tree-sitter -- no embeddings, no vector store. Every node is a code entity read straight from a syntax tree (module/class/function/method); every edge is tagged EXTRACTED (a fact read directly from a single source site: an import statement, a call site, a base class) or INFERRED (resolved by traversing the graph across files/scopes, or by an optional configured semantic API pass). `omni graph trace <a> <b>` answers 'how are these connected' with an actual shortest path of tagged hops instead of a similarity score; `omni graph show <node>` lists a symbol's direct EXTRACTED/INFERRED edges. Covers Python, JavaScript, and TypeScript in v1. tree-sitter and the per-language grammars are an optional `[graph]` extra so the workspace stays dependency-free by default: `omni graph build` fails with an actionable install message if the extra is missing, while `trace`/`show` only read the JSON `build` wrote and need nothing beyond the standard library. The semantic pass is opt-in via `--semantic` and only calls out to a network API if OMNI_GRAPH_SEMANTIC_API_URL is explicitly configured; its findings are still validated against known graph symbol names before being added as INFERRED edges, so a hallucinated relation can't be written into the graph silently. The CLI surface (subcommand-per-verb, a --json mode on every command) is intentionally 1:1 wrappable by an MCP relay the same way omni_map/omni_doctor/omni_sync already are.
acceptance_criteria: omni graph build parses Python, JavaScript, and TypeScript source with tree-sitter and writes a JSON graph whose edges are each tagged provenance EXTRACTED or INFERRED, with a resolver field distinguishing syntax / graph-traversal / semantic-api.

omni graph build fails with a clear install message (not a traceback) when tree-sitter or a language grammar is missing, verified by running it against the system Python with no [graph] extra installed.

omni graph trace <a> <b> resolves symbol names (preferring real symbols over unresolved external placeholders on a name collision) and prints the shortest path between them as a sequence of tagged hops; ambiguous or missing names are reported, not guessed.
omni graph show <node> lists a symbol's direct outgoing and incoming edges with provenance tags.

Cross-file call/import/inheritance resolution (INFERRED edges) verified against this repository's own make_ai.py plus a scratch TypeScript fixture with a cross-file import, confirming resolved edges are correct and that common built-ins (e.g. print) are excluded from the ambiguous unique-name fallback.
omni graph build/trace/show and the graph JSON never require network access unless --semantic is passed and OMNI_GRAPH_SEMANTIC_API_URL is set.
omni doctor gained a non-blocking check that only validates the graph file's JSON shape when one is present, since building the graph is opt-in.
pyproject.toml exposes tree-sitter + grammars as an optional [graph] extra rather than a hard dependency.
risk_notes: Call/inheritance resolution uses deterministic heuristics (same-module lookup, import-alias resolution, unique-name-in-graph fallback) rather than full type inference; ambiguous or dynamically-dispatched references are correctly left EXTRACTED-only rather than guessed, which is intentional but means some real connections will not surface as INFERRED edges in v1.
Nested function/class definitions declared inside another function's body are attributed to the enclosing function rather than modeled as their own node, to keep v1's traversal bounded.

The semantic pass sends a symbol's name, qualified name, and the full list of known symbol qualified_names to the configured API; it is opt-in (--semantic flag plus an explicitly set OMNI_GRAPH_SEMANTIC_API_URL) so nothing leaves the machine by default.

requirements.title: Restyle OmniEngineering's brand assets to match the ctxrelay/PathBox family

Replaced OmniEngineering's assets with a new set in that same family -- assets/brand/omni-mark.svg, omni-wordmark.svg, omni-banner.svg -- keeping the shared chrome (panel, corner nodes, beacon, banner grid/mesh/scanline/signature) pixel-identical to the siblings and giving OmniEngineering its own mark content: a central hub fanned out to five small nodes, representing the actual product (one repo-local .ai/ control plane synced out to many AI assistant entrypoints), distinct from CtxRelay's two-endpoint relay and PathBox's chat panel. The wordmark uses the literal `omni` CLI name rather than the full 'OmniEngineering' repo name, matching how the sibling brands use their short product/command name.

The old assets/banners/ and assets/identity/ directories and their omniengineering-*.svg files are removed.
README.md's top banner and its 'optional presentation assets' listing point at assets/brand/ instead of the removed directories.
make_ai.py's ADOPTION_PRESENTATION_FILES points at assets/brand instead of the removed assets/identity and assets/banners paths, so omni adopt --include-presentation still works.
.gitignore no longer excludes assets/brand/ (it silently ignored this exact directory since a June 2026 commit, which would have made the new canonical brand assets untrackable).
omni doctor and omni map both run clean after the change (the architecture diagram at assets/omni-context.svg, which doctor validates by name, is untouched).

The functional architecture diagrams under design/diagrams/ and assets/omni-context.svg were intentionally left in their existing style since they illustrate mechanism, not brand identity, and the request was scoped to 'the look', not every diagram in the repo.

Verified the new SVGs render correctly (matching structure/behavior to the already-shipped sibling files) via a local cairosvg render; a font-fallback rendering artifact on the monospace wordmark text appeared identically on PathBox's own shipped wordmark under the same renderer, confirming it is a local missing-font rendering quirk and not a defect introduced here.

requirements.title: Fix: adopting or updating omni_graph.py must not be able to break every other command
requirements.description: Found by end-to-end testing REQ-015 against a simulated pre-existing application: (1) ADOPTION_CLI_FILES only listed omni/make_ai.py, so `omni adopt --include-cli` copied a make_ai.py that unconditionally imports omni_graph without ever copying omni_graph.py itself, crashing every single omni command (not just `graph`) in the adopted project with a raw ModuleNotFoundError. (2) Testing the upgrade path (a project adopted before omni_graph.py existed, running `omni update` against a source that now has it) surfaced a deeper, structural gap: `omni update`'s file list (TEMPLATE_MANAGED_FILES) is evaluated by the OLD make_ai.py that is currently running the update, not by the newer --source -- so a target can never discover a brand-new template-managed file on the very first update after it's introduced, no matter what that file list contains by the time of a *later* update. Fixed both: added omni_graph.py to ADOPTION_CLI_FILES (fixes fresh `omni adopt --include-cli` immediately, and fixes `omni update` from the second update onward once a target is running post-fix code), and made make_ai.py's own `import omni_graph` defensive (try/except, falls back to None) with a shared require_omni_graph() guard on every `omni graph ...` subcommand and a doctor warning -- so a target still missing omni_graph.py (the unavoidable one-time gap on that very first update, or any other reason the file might be absent) degrades to 'omni graph is unavailable' instead of taking down doctor/sync/map/every other command.
acceptance_criteria: omni adopt --target <dir> --include-cli copies omni_graph.py alongside make_ai.py, verified against a scratch pre-existing application directory whose own pre-existing files (README, source, .gitignore) are confirmed byte-for-byte unchanged after adoption.

A project simulated as adopted before omni_graph.py existed (sourced from OmniEngineering@523c47b) that runs `omni update` against a current source no longer crashes: omni doctor, omni sync, and every non-graph command work immediately after that update even though omni_graph.py is still absent on that specific first pass, with a clear doctor warning naming the gap and the fix (re-run omni adopt --include-cli or omni update).

The same project's second `omni update` (now running the fixed make_ai.py) reports 'added: omni_graph.py', after which omni graph build/trace/show all work against the adopted project's own source files.

Adopter-owned files (.ai/project-configuration.md, .ai/project-map.md, .ai/requirements/requirements.json, CHANGELOG.md) verified untouched by both update passes in this test, including a deliberately added custom note/entry in each.
omni doctor and omni graph both continue to work correctly in this repo's own working copy (which always has omni_graph.py) after these changes.
risk_notes: The structural update-mechanism gap (a target's own running code decides what files it looks for) is not fully eliminated -- it is closed for every template file added from this point forward (once a target has updated past this fix, it will correctly discover any future new template file on the very next update), but a project that adopted before omni_graph.py existed will still see one warning-but-not-broken update before omni_graph.py actually arrives. A fully general fix would have run_update ask --source's own make_ai.py for its current file manifest via subprocess instead of trusting its own constant; deferred as a larger structural change beyond this fix's scope.

The defensive import is the durable half of this fix: it guarantees a missing omni_graph.py (for this reason or any other -- a bad copy, manual deletion) degrades to one feature being unavailable rather than the whole CLI being unusable, independent of whether the file-list gap above is ever fully closed.

requirements.title: Replace the hierarchical code-map diagram with a real node-link graph
requirements.description: The first design/diagrams/omni-code-map.svg (REQ-015 follow-up) was a hierarchical org-chart-style diagram (boxes, arrows, a text-list panel for doctor checks) built from omni graph build's own output. User feedback: it didn't read as 'a graph' in the conventional sense. Replaced it with design/diagrams/omni-code-graph.svg -- a real force-directed node-link layout (networkx spring_layout) over all 106 real (non-external) symbols and 277 resolved calls/defines edges from the same .ai/project-graph.json, rendered as circles (sized by kind, colored by source module) and lines (calls vs. defines distinguished). No fabricated structure: same underlying data, different -- and correctly graph-shaped -- visual form.
acceptance_criteria: design/diagrams/omni-code-map.svg (the org-chart version) is removed.
design/diagrams/omni-code-graph.svg exists, is well-formed XML, and renders as a force-directed node-link graph (verified via a local cairosvg render) rather than a hierarchical chart.
README's Design Documents list points at the new file with an accurate description.
risk_notes: Generating this diagram required networkx + numpy for the spring layout; these are one-off diagram-authoring tools, not a runtime dependency of omni_graph.py or the [graph] extra, so nothing was added to pyproject.toml.

requirements.title: Add omni graph render: a permanent, stdlib-only SVG visualization command
requirements.description: REQ-018's node-link graph was a one-off script requiring networkx+numpy, run by hand and copied into the repo. User ask: this should be a permanent feature of omni itself that updates as the user's project updates, not a one-off artifact. Added `omni graph render` (and the underlying omni_graph.render()/_spring_layout()/_render_svg()/_ego_network() functions): renders .ai/project-graph.json as a force-directed node-link SVG using a small pure-Python Fruchterman-Reingold layout -- no numpy/networkx dependency, so render works with just the standard library exactly like trace/show (only build needs the [graph] extra). Nodes are colored by source language (python/javascript/typescript) and sized by kind (module > class > function/method); edges distinguish calls/imports/inherits (colored, per edge style) from defines (faint, de-emphasized) from related_to (dashed, semantic-pass edges). --max-nodes caps large graphs to the highest-degree nodes to keep the O(n^2) layout fast; --focus/--depth renders just one symbol's neighborhood instead of the whole codebase. design/diagrams/omni-code-graph.svg was regenerated using this actual shipped command (replacing the prior one-off script's output) so the committed diagram is proof the feature works, not just a description of it.
acceptance_criteria: omni graph render writes a well-formed SVG node-link graph from .ai/project-graph.json, verified by parsing the output as XML and rendering it to PNG for visual review.
render works via plain system Python with no tree-sitter or third-party layout library installed, verified by running it without the [graph] extra present.

Layout performance verified empirically: 112 real nodes rendered in ~0.2s, 300 nodes (max-nodes cap, including external references) in ~1.3s against this repo's own graph -- fast enough for normal CLI use.
--focus <symbol> --depth N renders only that symbol's N-hop neighborhood, verified against run_doctor at depth 1 producing a correct, legible ego-network.
--max-nodes correctly truncates to the highest-degree nodes and reports truncated:true, verified by rendering with include_external=True against a cap below the real node count.
The project's own root label in the rendered title resolves to a real folder name instead of a literal '.', verified before and after the fix.
design/diagrams/omni-code-graph.svg in this repo is the literal output of running `omni graph render` against this repo, not a hand-tuned or separately-scripted render.

omni doctor and omni graph build/trace/show continue to pass after these changes; .ai/project-graph.svg (the default output path) is gitignored the same way .ai/project-graph.json is, since it's a heavy, regeneratable, opt-in artifact, not a committed navigation aid.
risk_notes: The layout is O(n^2) per iteration (a deliberate simplicity/dependency tradeoff over numpy-vectorized force-directed algorithms), which is why --max-nodes defaults to 300 and truncates by degree rather than rendering arbitrarily large graphs unbounded.

Dense, highly-connected clusters (e.g. this repo's own doctor-validator cluster) still show some label overlap at default settings -- an inherent characteristic of force-directed layouts at this node density, not something --max-nodes or --focus fully eliminates; --focus on a smaller neighborhood is the escape hatch for a specific area.

requirements.title: Make completion enforcement real: executable gates, registry CLI, typed validation, config-driven banner
requirements.description: Rulepack validation blocks were never executed and omni doctor checked that registry keys existed but never their types, so assistants could skip changelog/registry updates and hand-write malformed requirement entries (25 schema violations in one adopter) without any check failing. The 531 KB adopter registry was also pushed into every context profile. Adds omni gate (co_changed rule execution against the git change set plus doctor errors) with auditable waivers and a Claude Code Stop hook, requirement show/list/search/update/complete/archive so nobody reads or hand-edits the registry JSON, type and enum validation of the registry and its archive, and config-driven classification_banner and allowed_root_paths.

Attribution: NOTICE, .ai/graph-viewer/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md generated from each package's own license file, and the same notices embedded in every generated page.

headless Chromium WebGL run with search and select and expand and isolate and screenshots

Verified by plain ./omni graph build from a system Python without tree-sitter and by the failure path with HOME pointed at an empty directory.

requirements.title: Cut manual process: draft requirements/changelog from a commit, and rebuild the graph on commit
requirements.description: Two of the workspace's remaining manual steps: (1) omni requirement draft [--commit REF] infers a category from the changed paths, takes the title from the commit subject (or a placeholder), and writes a proposed (never completed) requirement plus a matching CHANGELOG.md Proposed stub, so review replaces hand-authoring; it refuses to draft a duplicate when the commit message already cites a requirement ID. (2) omni hook install-git --with-graph-rebuild adds a post-commit hook that rebuilds the graph in the background after every commit (a lock directory skips an overlapping run; output goes to .ai/.graph-build.log; a full rebuild never blocks git commit, which matters since a real rebuild can take well over a minute on a large repo).

requirements.title: Make declared rule validations real: a dead check fixed, one new honest safety net added
requirements.description: gate_rules() only ever selected validation.type == co_changed, so controlled.requirement_id's declared requirement_registry_entry validation was silently never executed -- a rule that looked machine-checked but was not. Fixed by implementing it for real: every REQ-###-shaped ID cited in a commit message since the base, or newly added to CHANGELOG.md, must exist in the registry (catches a typo'd/invented id that the registry's own schema validation cannot see, since that only checks the registry's own shape). Added one new, honestly-scoped validation type, content_forbidden: changed files are scanned for a short list of regexes (private-key header, AWS-shaped access key, obviously hardcoded credential), applied to data.privacy. Deliberately did not try to mechanize the other ~55 unvalidated rules (cognitive load, composition vs inheritance, naming, ...): those are real judgment calls with no honest mechanical proxy, and faking one would be worse than leaving it a judgment call. EXECUTABLE_VALIDATION_TYPES now documents the matched pair (gate_rules selection + gate_evaluate dispatch) so a new type added to one and not the other fails loudly instead of silently doing nothing, which is exactly the bug this fixes.

requirements.title: omni graph benchmark: measure the token-savings claim instead of just asserting it
requirements.description: omni graph benchmark [--json] runs a targeted graph query (why/lineage) against the naive alternative (grep -l -F for the name, then read every matching file whole; a commit compares against git show, the actual diff) for one real requirement, commit, failure and file the current project's own graph and registries already have -- never invented, never hardcoded to a specific project's IDs, so any adopter gets their own honest numbers. Tokens are reported as chars/4, explicitly labelled a rough estimate, not a real tokenizer. Two data-quality bugs were found and fixed while building this: the file case first picked a 290MB gitignored .expo build log (a generic 'file' graph node existed for it despite it being gitignored), then a 5.5MB .pptx after tracked-only filtering (a binary asset). Fixed by restricting the file pick to git-tracked, already-parsed source modules only -- never a generic file node, which can be a binary or an ignored artifact.
